title: Kurt Burris: Oklahoma Center and 1954 Heisman Runner-Up
question: Which Oklahoma center finished second in the 1954 Heisman Trophy voting?
answer: Kurt Burris, a center and linebacker who played for Oklahoma from 1951 to 1954, finished second to Wisconsin's Alan Ameche in the 1954 Heisman Trophy vote. He was also a consensus All-American that season and was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2000.
summary: Kurt Burris, Oklahoma's center and linebacker, finished second to Alan Ameche in the 1954 Heisman voting and was a consensus All-American that year.
body: Heisman voters rarely look toward the middle of the offensive line, but in 1954 they did. Oklahoma's Kurt Burris, a center who also played linebacker, finished second in the voting to Wisconsin fullback Alan Ameche, according to the College Football Hall of Fame.

Burris played for the Sooners from 1951 to 1954, in the one-platoon era when a center was expected to snap the ball on offense and then take a defensive position as a linebacker. The Hall of Fame notes that Oklahoma went 35-4-2 over his four seasons, and he was named all-conference in 1953 and 1954.

His senior year brought the biggest honors. Burris was a consensus All-American in 1954. The Helms Foundation named him its player of the year, and the Philadelphia Sports Writers Association chose him as its lineman of the year.

Burris grew up in Muskogee, one of 11 children, in a family that sent several sons to college football. Buddy Burris, a three-time Sooner All-American in the late 1940s, was his brother. After football Kurt moved to Billings, Montana, where he became president of an oil and gas company and took part in civic work.

The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 2000. For fans looking for Oklahoma legends beyond the famous backs and quarterbacks, Burris is a good example of how much a lineman can mean to a team.
